comment: cowdiff states for f_100dc0a0 (cow_net_clock_minutes) - read and PROVEN, but the entry has no owner: nothing in the image calls it or stores its address (callers_of.py 0 and refs_to.py 0, and it is not a slot of any table), so the loop's no-stub rule keeps it out of the ledger's done set. These states are here so that when something turns out to reach it, the proof is already written. The entry's answer is (seconds x 60) - trunc(ms_accum x -0.06), and the two things worth naming are the accumulator's magnitude (the scaling is a double multiply and the game's own conversion truncates toward zero, so a wide value shows a conversion that rounded, or that widened wrongly) and the fact that eax and edx leave holding the SAME difference (0x100dc0d5-0x100dc0d9). The clock pointer is pinned because a fuzzed one faults at the first field read and both sides would agree on nothing. Bytes are RAW little-endian.

states.note: 5 s and 1000 ms: 300 - trunc(1000 x -0.06 = -60) = 360, in both eax and edx

0 s and 0xffffffff ms: the accumulator as an unsigned 32-bit integer scaled into a large negative double and truncated toward zero - the high half of the int64 is what makes edx differ from eax's own low bits before the final mov
1 s and 0 ms: the answer is exactly 60 - and the qword's high half had to be written 0 by the entry at 0x100dc0aa (the state leaves that memory fuzzed), or fild would have converted garbage
